name: Bassem Boules
heroTitle:
Portraits drawn
out of the dark.
heroNote: Move your light across the drawing
intro: Egyptian artist and illustrator, trained in the Faculty of Fine Arts at Alexandria University and working in Dubai. I draw the way the Old Masters taught: slowly, from light and shadow, until a face starts looking back.

works.title: Eye Study I
works.story: Charcoal makes the eye come alive. One of a pair of studies built from soft charcoal, a blending stump and the white of the paper.

works.title: Idris Elba
works.story: Painted with a single oil flat brush with thick bristles, keeping every stroke visible in the beard and skin.

works.title: Wdn Al Ota
works.story: “The cat's ear”: the Egyptian nickname for molokhia leaves, because of their shape. A kitchen in Egypt, a bowl of soup and a cat who knows exactly what it wants.

works.title: Tear
works.story: A study of a single eye: wet lashes, a green-grey iris and one tear leaving a trail across the skin.

works.title: Between the Past and Future
works.story: A woman in a red kandora and gold-trimmed burqa reaches for an old lantern while the Dubai skyline waits, half drawn, behind her. Made at Tashkeel.

works.title: Eye Study II
works.story: The companion study: lashes drawn one by one, and the window light reflected in the iris.

works.title: Classic Soft Pastel Portrait
works.story: A large portrait built up by hand in layers of soft pastel.

works.title: Fairouz
works.story: The singer drawn in thousands of engraved lines of riso blue, overprinted with Ibrahim Zaki's red Arabic lettering. Shown in Khali Balak Men RISO at Tashkeel.

works.title: Eye Study
works.story: Each wrinkle and texture tells a story.

works.title: Eight Hours of Charcoal
works.story: A cat in eight hours of charcoal, finished fur by fur with a white pencil.

works.title: Mona Zaki
works.story: A portrait of the Egyptian actress, painted in four and a half hours.

works.title: A Day in Dubai
works.story: The Museum of the Future, Dubai Frame, Burj Al Arab and Burj Khalifa in one afternoon. Each colour is a separate pass through the riso machine; the print took about two hours.

works.title: Pencil Study
works.medium: Mechanical pencil, charcoal and soft powder
works.story: Drawn with a fine mechanical pencil over a charcoal and powder base.

works.title: Teaching Study
works.story: Painted live for a class, to show how the eye is built from shapes of warm and cool colour.

works.title: The Pantocrator
works.story: Christ as the Alpha and the Omega, in the tradition of Coptic icon painting.

detail.quote: Each wrinkle and texture tells a story.

teaching.title: The workshop table
teaching.text: I teach drawing, portraiture, pastel and risograph at Tashkeel in Dubai, for children, families and adults. The method is the same at every level: look longer, measure honestly, and let light and shadow do the work.
